top_choice_rationale: P002 rewards a complete theory-experiment loop: the Bistritzer-MacDonald continuum-model prediction of flat bands at a magic angle, tested seven years later by the observation of correlated insulating and superconducting states at that angle, reproduced in many laboratories and extended to other moire platforms, in a field with no earlier prize. I accept that the pairing mechanism is open, that twist-angle disorder matters, and that the three-name limit omits Cao and earlier twisted-bilayer theory, so the citation must stay narrow. P001 is a very close second: the lattice clock is mature, independently intercompared and has cleaner two-name credit, and its distinction from the 2005 and 2012 prizes is now clear to me. My preference is a judgement of category, not a flaw in that science. P000 is last because both awards are scientifically sound.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; as a computational condensed-matter theorist I have no listed tie to the B001 or B007 candidates, though electronic-structure work on moire systems is in my broad field
